newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Four sentenced to death in Vietnam graft trial.
newsitem.headline: Four sentenced to death in Vietnam graft trial.

text.p: A court in southern Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City has sentenced four people to death at the end of the communist country's biggest corruption trial, a court official said on Friday.
The official said one other defendant had been sentenced to life imprisonment, but was unable to immediately provide details of verdicts for 15 remaining defendants.

The trial, which had become a showcase for Hanoi's anti-graft resolve, centred around allegations of corruption at Ho Chi Minh City firm Tamexco, a trading company affiliated to the ruling Communist Party.

Earlier this week the lead defendants had pled for their lives to be spared. Defence lawyers had argued that they were victims of a lax administrative environment in Vietnam which allowed corruption to flourish.
Local journalists, who were allowed to attend the trial, named Tamexco director, Pham Huy Phuoc, as being among those sentenced to death by firing squad.
The others were named as local company directors Tran Quang Vinh and Le Minh Hai, and the head of a state notary office, Le Duc Canh.
